_note: Curriculum extracted from the BITS Pilani WILP M.Tech AIML programme brochure. Syllabus strings are verbatim from the brochure where available; courses with syllabus:null are listed in the brochure by title only.

groups.label: Electives — Audio & Vision
groups.hint: min. 3, incl. Audio Analysis / Computer Vision

courses.name: Mathematical Foundations for Machine Learning
courses.syllabus: Linear algebra, calculus, probability and optimisation as used by machine learning. The brochure does not print a detailed syllabus for this course; the pages below cover the algebra and linear algebra that everything else is built on, and the gradient descent page comes from its optimisation sessions.

courses.name: Machine Learning
courses.syllabus: Introduction to Machine Learning; various kinds of learning; supervised and unsupervised learning; the ML workflow; Bayesian learning, MAP hypothesis, Bayes optimal classifier, naive Bayes; linear models for regression; linear models for classification; non-linear models; decision trees; MDL principle; instance based learning; support vector machines; ensemble learning; clustering, k-means, GMM; model evaluation and comparison.

courses.name: Deep Neural Networks
courses.syllabus: Introduction to neural networks; linear neural networks for regression and classification; deep feedforward networks; backpropagation; deep network training; regularization and optimization; transfer learning and fine-tuning; convolutional neural networks; recurrent neural networks; attention mechanisms; transformers and vision transformers.
courses.note: The brochure prints this course under Semester 2. It sits here under Semester 1 because that is when the sessions are actually running — the syllabus above is still the published one, word for word.

courses.name: AI and ML Techniques for Cyber Security
courses.syllabus: AI and ML in cybersecurity; vulnerabilities, threats, attack vectors and defence strategies; vulnerability management using gradient boosting; code security and vulnerability detection through graph-based static analysis; graph neural networks for malware call graphs and attack paths; malware detection and classification; phishing and email security using NLP and transformers; network security monitoring; user and entity behaviour analytics with autoencoders; adversarial machine learning; GenAI and LLMs in security operations; automated response using reinforcement learning.

courses.name: Advanced Data Mining
courses.syllabus: Foundations of data mining and record data mining; association analysis and pattern discovery; mining complex data structures; tree and graph mining; sequence mining; web and text data mining; stream data mining; spatiotemporal data mining; multivariate time series; high-dimensional clustering; mining social networking sites; multi-relational data mining; privacy preserving data mining; distributed computing for data-intensive mining.

courses.name: Architecting AI Systems
courses.syllabus: End-to-end AI system design and architecture patterns; AI system components; architectural styles; agentic AI architecture; ADLC; MCP/A2A gateways and agent protocols; system-level design principles; scalability patterns; performance optimization; resiliency patterns; domain-specific blueprints; infrastructure integration; production considerations; governance.

courses.name: Agentic AI Systems
courses.syllabus: Foundations of agentic AI; industry use cases; LLMs as autonomous agents; prompt engineering for agents; ReAct, Plan-and-Execute and Reflexion agents; memory and context management; knowledge-grounded agentic systems; multi-agent systems and collaboration; safety, governance and explainability; evaluation, deployment and MLOps; building a goal-driven LLM agent with tool calling.

courses.name: Introduction to Parallel and Distributed Programming
Multimodal AI
courses.syllabus: Foundations of multi-modal ML; different input modalities; multimodal fusion and fission; multimodal models and pretraining; cross-modal alignment and grounding; visual understanding and reasoning; generative multimodal AI; temporal intelligence; embodied AI; ethics and safety; advanced topics.

courses.name: Advanced Reasoning and Planning
courses.syllabus: Introduction to reasoning and planning; LLM reasoning; large reasoning models; reasoning-oriented prompting; inference-time scaling; verification; RL for reasoning; knowledge representation and memory; hybrid reasoning; LLM-based planning; multi-LLM collaboration; evaluation, safety and state of the art.

courses.name: Conversational AI
courses.syllabus: Design and build conversational AI agents that think, plan and act autonomously. Intelligent systems using large language models, memory, tool integration and information retrieval. Production skills: system architecture, security, ethical considerations, cost optimization and performance monitoring. Design, implement, evaluate and deploy scalable agents for enterprise applications.

courses.name: Large Language Models for Generative AI
courses.syllabus: Foundations of large language models; pre-trained LLMs; inference; fine-tuning techniques; preference alignment; prompt engineering and reasoning; scaling and optimizing LLMs; retrieval-augmented and retrieval-enhanced language models; LLMs as agents; structured data handling; evaluation; challenges; security and privacy; advanced topics.

courses.name: NLP Applications
courses.syllabus: Sentiment analysis and opinion mining; machine translation including Indic languages; question answering and conversational AI; information extraction; knowledge graph and RAG applications; security, privacy and ethics in NLP; scalable and efficient NLP systems; implementing these applications with current generative and agentic AI technologies.

courses.name: Social Media Analytics
courses.syllabus: Social media data collection, preprocessing and analysis over noisy, unstructured, multimodal data. Social network analysis, influencer detection, sentiment analysis and trend discovery to understand user behaviour and information diffusion. Multimodal analytics and visualization. Security: fake account, bot, spam and misinformation detection. Governance: data privacy, ethical use and regulatory compliance.

courses.name: Audio Analysis
courses.syllabus: Audio fundamentals and feature extraction; acoustic AI applications (healthcare monitoring, industrial predictive maintenance, ultrasound); deep learning models for audio (CNNs, RNNs/LSTMs, audio transformers); classification and tagging; speech-language models (ASR, TTS, voice assistants); music analysis and recommendation; audio-language models; audio generation; agentic AI for audio; ethics and privacy.

courses.name: Computer Vision
courses.syllabus: Introduction to computer vision and applications; vision fundamentals; image features (edges, corners, texture, keypoint descriptors); CNNs for vision; classification architectures (ResNet, EfficientNet); object detection (YOLO, R-CNN families); semantic and instance segmentation (U-Net, Mask R-CNN); vision transformers; image generation (GANs, diffusion); vision-language models; captioning; visual question answering; agentic AI for vision; ethics and privacy.

courses.name: Video Analysis
courses.syllabus: Video fundamentals (spatial, temporal and motion features, optical flow, spatio-temporal features); temporal and spatio-temporal models (3D CNNs, video transformers); action recognition and temporal action detection; video object detection and tracking; segmentation; anomaly and deepfake detection; captioning and video question answering; video generation; summarization; agentic AI for video; ethics and privacy.

courses.name: Dissertation
courses.syllabus: A workplace or industry project in the final semester: apply the programme to a complex real problem and demonstrate command of the concepts.

algebra.label: Algebra
algebra.blurb: A letter is just a box you have not filled in yet. Build a rule, then stack two rules and watch a curve appear.

linalg.label: Linear algebra
linalg.blurb: A matrix is a machine that moves every arrow in the plane at once. Bend space with four numbers.

regression.label: Linear regression
regression.blurb: Drag a line through a cloud of dots and watch the error rise and fall.

gradient.label: Gradient descent
gradient.blurb: Roll downhill in fog. Push the step size until the whole thing explodes.

kmeans.label: k-means clustering
kmeans.blurb: Plant k flags, everyone joins the nearest one, flags move. Step through it.

mllec1.label: Lecture 1 — Introduction to Machine Learning
mllec1.blurb: What machine learning is, when it is worth using, and the three kinds of it. Write a task as ⟨T, P, E⟩, drag a decision boundary, and watch an agent learn by being rewarded.

mllec2.label: Lecture 2 — The machine learning workflow: data and preprocessing
mllec2.blurb: Where the time actually goes. Attribute types, dirty data, outliers, sampling, scaling and encoding — the whole of module M2.

attrtypes.label: Levels of measurement: nominal, ordinal, interval, ratio
attrtypes.blurb: Four questions decide what a column means, and which sums on it are honest.

scaling.label: Feature scaling: normalisation and standardisation
scaling.blurb: Two ways to make columns comparable, and the rule about fitting them that decides whether your score is real.

encoding.label: Turning categories into numbers
encoding.blurb: One-hot and label encoding. One invents an order that is not there; the other does not.

hypothesis.label: Hypotheses, the hypothesis space and version space
hypothesis.blurb: What a learner is actually searching, from the most specific ∅ to the most general ?.

perceptron.label: The perceptron
perceptron.blurb: One neuron rotating a line into place, one mistake at a time.

neuron.label: The artificial neuron
neuron.blurb: Weights, a sum and a decision. Drag three weights and watch one number decide the answer — the same dot product you met in the maths course, wearing a different hat.

linsep.label: Linear separability and the decision boundary
linsep.blurb: When one straight line is enough, and what it costs when it is not. Move a boundary through thirteen points, then meet the four points no line can ever split.

lossfn.label: Objective functions: what learning actually minimises
lossfn.blurb: Lower is better, by convention. Compare squared error against error rate on the same predictions and watch them disagree about which model is best.

activation.label: Activation functions: the bend that makes depth worth having
activation.blurb: The step that cannot be trained, the identity that changes nothing, and the shapes in between. Stack two layers with each and watch which ones collapse.

metrics.label: Scoring a regression: MSE, RMSE, MAE and R²
metrics.blurb: Four numbers about the same predictions. Drag one point to the far end and watch which of them notice.

designmat.label: The design matrix, and predicting a whole dataset at once
designmat.blurb: Glue a column of ones onto your data and the bias becomes an ordinary weight. Then every prediction in the set is one matrix multiply.

dl2.label: Session 2 — The perceptron
dl2.blurb: The same unit again, in the notation the rest of the course uses: z = Σwᵢxᵢ + b, then an activation. Solve the gates in the 0/1 encoding, run the learning algorithm with a separate bias update, and keep the four output conventions straight.

dl3.label: Session 3 — Linear neural networks for regression
dl3.blurb: One neuron with no bend at all. Build the design matrix, write the squared-error loss, take its gradient, and follow the deck's own numerical example from a loss of 7.5 down to 1.51 in a single step.

dl1.label: Session 1 — Fundamentals of Neural Networks
dl1.blurb: What makes learning deep, the four parts every deep learning problem has, and the single neuron the whole field is built on. Solve a logic gate by hand, train one with the perceptron rule, then find the gate that breaks it and fix it with a hidden layer.

matmul.label: Multiplying matrices
matmul.blurb: Row of one meets column of the other. Press a number in the answer and watch both light up — then find two matrices that multiply to zero without either being zero.

determinant.label: The determinant and the inverse
determinant.blurb: One number that says whether a matrix can be undone. Drag two arrows until the box between them goes flat and watch the inverse disappear.

rank.label: Rank: how much your data really says
rank.blurb: Copy one row onto another and watch the count drop. Then compare two ranks and read off whether a system has no answer, one, or endlessly many.

dotproduct.label: The dot product: length, angle and shadow
dotproduct.blurb: Multiply matching parts and add. One number that gives you length, the angle between two vectors, a cheap test for right angles, and the shadow one casts on another.

covariance.label: Spread, and whether two things move together
covariance.blurb: Variance as squares you can grow, then covariance as one rectangle per point — teal when the two rise together, red when they pull apart.

vectorspace.label: Vector spaces and subspaces
vectorspace.blurb: A set you cannot fall out of. Drag two answers until their sum leaves the line, then try to break six candidate subsets and find which promise each one fails.

basis.label: Span, basis and dimension
basis.blurb: What a handful of vectors can reach, whether any of them is carrying nothing, and why every honest shelf for the same space has the same length.

lec0a.label: Lecture 0a — Matrices, determinants and linear systems
lec0a.blurb: The toolkit the rest of the course is built from. Multiply matrices by pressing a number and seeing where it came from, drag two arrows until the determinant hits zero, then turn [A | I] into [I | A⁻¹] one move at a time.

lec0b.label: Lecture 0b — Vectors, dot products and probability
lec0b.blurb: Two halves that turn out to be the same idea. Drag arrows until they stop being independent, get a dot product to land on exactly zero, then meet random variables, expectation and covariance — where the covariance is drawn as one rectangle per data point.

lec1.label: Lecture 1 — Linear equations & Gaussian elimination
lec1.blurb: Straight-line rules that must all hold at once. Drag two lines to see why there are only ever three outcomes, then solve any system one legal move at a time.

lec2.label: Lecture 2 — Vector spaces, independence and basis
lec2.blurb: What a space has to promise before you can call it one. Break a subset by dragging until a sum falls outside it, watch a span collapse from a plane to a line, and end on the deck's own unfinished example — worked out and checked.

lec3.label: Lecture 3 — Analytic geometry
lec3.blurb: Length, distance and angle, built from one new object: the inner product. Change the inner product and watch two vectors stop being at right angles, then build an orthonormal basis by elimination.

ism1.label: Lecture 1 — Describing data: centre, spread and outliers
ism1.blurb: Drag dots on a line and watch the mean chase them while the median stays put. Then square the distances, find the quartiles, and see what counts as an outlier.

ism2.label: Lecture 2 — Probability: events, axioms and the addition rule
ism2.blurb: Drag two circles until they overlap and watch the addition rule explain itself. Then roll 36 dice outcomes, test the axioms, and sort out independent from mutually exclusive.

ism3.label: Lecture 3 — Conditional probability, independence and Bayes
ism3.blurb: News arrives and the odds move. Shrink the sample space onto what you were told, chain the multiplication rule down a tree, then split the world into slices and turn the last one round with Bayes.

centre.label: Averages: mean, median and mode
centre.blurb: Three answers to "where is the middle?". Drag one dot to the far end and see which of them chases it.

spread.label: Spread: how far apart the numbers are
spread.blurb: Two sets can share a mean and have nothing else in common. Square the distances and watch why one odd value dominates.

outliers.label: Outliers and the box plot
outliers.blurb: Five numbers describe a whole dataset. Put up the fences and drag a value past one.

probability.label: Probability: what the number actually means
probability.blurb: Count the outcomes, or run it a thousand times. Two definitions of the same number, and they meet in the middle.

events.label: Events as sets: and, or, not
events.blurb: Every probability question is a set question first. Build events by hand, then let area do the arithmetic.

conditional.label: Conditional probability: what a probability does when you learn something
conditional.blurb: Being told something happened throws away part of the sample space. Shade the part that survives and watch the number move.

bayes.label: Total probability and Bayes' rule
bayes.blurb: Split the world into slices, add up the routes to an event, then run the last arrow backwards to ask which slice you came from.

lec4.label: Lecture 4 — Eigenvalues & eigenvectors
lec4.blurb: The directions a matrix cannot turn. Expand a determinant by cofactors, put a letter on the diagonal to get the characteristic polynomial, then find the vectors that only get stretched — and end with the two decompositions those vectors build: A = QΛQᵀ and A = LLᵀ.

eigen.label: Eigenvalues and eigenvectors
eigen.blurb: Most vectors get turned. A few only get stretched, and those few tell you what the matrix really does. Drag one round a circle until it stops turning.

spectraldecomp.label: The spectral decomposition: A = QΛQᵀ
spectraldecomp.blurb: A symmetric matrix pulled apart into a rotation, a stretch and the rotation undone. Build Q and Λ, multiply them back, and check you get what you started with.

trace.label: The trace
trace.blurb: Add up the diagonal and stop. One number, four rules, and the one that surprises people: tr(AB) = tr(BA) even when AB and BA are different sizes.

cholesky.label: Cholesky decomposition
cholesky.blurb: The square root of a matrix, when the matrix is symmetric and positive definite. Six formulas, checked by multiplying back, and the sampling trick they exist for.
